# Lesson: LEFT JOIN keeps rows that have no match

**Concept:** LEFT JOIN  **Mission link:** predict which columns come back NULL

**Primary source:** PostgreSQL manual, "Joins Between Tables" (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/tutorial-join.html)

## Teach
An INNER JOIN drops a customer with no orders. `customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id` keeps that customer and fills every `o` column with NULL.

## Practice
Predict the NULL columns for a customer who has never ordered, then run it.

## Go deeper
Further reading: Use The Index, Luke, "The Join Operation". Ask me about anything unclear.

# Lesson: LEFT JOIN

This lesson follows one source: section 7.2.1.1 "Joined Tables" of the PostgreSQL manual. Everything below is checked against it.

## Teach
For each row of the left table, LEFT JOIN returns the joined row when the ON condition matches, and otherwise one row with NULLs for the right table's columns.

## Practice
Which `orders` columns are NULL for a customer with no orders?
